name: velocity-rewarding hybrid bass and impact
goal: Design a thunderous hybrid bass/impact that responds exponentially to velocity (louder hits open filter/amp dramatically), usable as deep hits or high atmospheric stabs with HP + long space reverb.

source.title: TRAVELER Track Walkthrough by Venus Theory

prerequisites: Hybrid synth or Traveler-inspired Web Audio engine with multi-osc, stereo filter, envelopes, LFOs/mod matrix, sequenced control tracks (or automation), and FX (EQ/chorus/delay/reverb)
constraints: Original synthesis only; not affiliated with KeySolutions; do not rip Traveler samples/presets/wavetables.
Original synthesis only — design new patches from portable parameters; do not copy proprietary Traveler factory preset names, banks, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with KeySolutions Sounds or Traveler; concepts mapped to generic hybrid-synth / Web Audio equivalents.
Do not rip, dump, or redistribute Traveler content.
Prefer recreating the described signal-flow and motion relationships in our browser music system or any hybrid synth with comparable modules.

steps.action: Start with dark hybrid oscillators (saw/pulse + optional WT). Fast amp attack, punchy decay, moderate sustain for bass; shorter for impacts.
Map velocity strongly (near-exponential) to filter cutoff and/or drive so louder playing blooms dramatically.
steps.expect: Soft vs hard hits differ a lot

steps.action: For atmospheric use: apply aggressive high-pass on the mix, play high register with pitch bend, and use a broad smooth space-style reverb so hits become huge pads/stingers.
steps.expect: High notes feel epic and layerable

steps.action: For deep bass: keep HP low/off, emphasize transient, optionally underscoring with sub; avoid static sine-only subs — keep some transient character.

verification: Low mode works as hybrid bass
